title: Format durations, calendar values and time points
problem: Format chrono values without host locale, timezone-database or strftime services.
design: Civil-date arithmetic and explicit tokens preserve device callability; locale/timezone queries remain unsupported.
tradeoffs:
The header supports durations, C++20 calendar values, `std::tm`, system time
points and local time points using civil-date arithmetic and explicit tokens.
Fractional precision, negative timestamps and ISO week years follow the pinned
fmt reference. This implementation provides locale-independent formatting; it
does not query clocks, a timezone database or locale services. Local time points
therefore reject zone/offset tokens. Device use requires the involved standard
chrono operations to be available on that device.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; duration/calendar/token/wide/rejection tests grouped, oracle calendar wrappers kept local. No implementation token change.

before: A std::chrono::milliseconds value has no formatter, so the %T token cannot produce a duration.

title: Opt enums into integer formatting
problem: Expose enum underlying values without globally accepting every enum.
design: Small ADL opt-in shares the integer parser and avoids symbolic-name reflection.
tradeoffs:
`ffmt::underlying(value)` explicitly exposes an enum's underlying integer.
Opting into `ffmt::enums::format_as` in the enum's namespace enables ADL mapping
with the integer formatter's specifications. This prints integer values rather
than discovering symbolic names. The opt-in avoids globally making every enum
formattable.

title: Test names with independent range and standard adapters
problem: Verify cross-feature composition without making optional adapters depend on each other.
design: Integration-only fixtures sit above independent feature branches.
tradeoffs:
Named argument wrappers preserve the referenced family's mutability and provide
runtime names for outer width fields. The interaction tests combine names with
ranges and standard-type adapters. Each family and named arguments also has an
independent test suite, so this integration adds no prerequisite between those
features.

title: Add referenced named arguments
problem: Resolve human-readable field names while retaining typed value references.
design: Name lookup is runtime; wrappers do not allocate or own their referents.
tradeoffs:
`ffmt::arg(name, value)` stores a name view and a value reference. The name
characters and value must outlive use of the wrapper; temporary values remain
valid through the formatting expression. Names and named width/precision fields
are resolved at runtime. Literal parsing checks structural syntax, but cannot
fully validate a named field's type/specification because names are runtime data.
Use checked results to observe unresolved names or incompatible specifications.

title: Format ranges, tuples and joins
problem: Format structured containers using element formatters while preserving iterator semantics.
design: Range detection and constrained formatter specializations; standard operations remain device-dependent.
tradeoffs:
Ranges select sequence, set, map, string or debug-string presentation. Tuples
and container adaptors have explicit adapters; nested specifications follow the
second colon, while `n` removes delimiters. `range_format_kind` customizes string
versus debug-string treatment. Joins hold iterator/delimiter views; keep their
underlying objects alive. Mutable and move-only input iterators are preserved.
Right/center alignment on streaming iterators requires repeatable element
formatters and forward ranges; bounded writable buffers handle consuming ranges
without replay. The standard-library operations used by the range must be
callable on the selected device.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; range/iterator/mutation tests extracted and grouped, cross-feature named-range assertion moved to integration. No implementation token change.

title: Share nested output accounting and family alignment
problem: Optional formatters need consistent nested alignment without buffering or replaying mutations.
design: Extend bounded sink iterators with padding marks/reordering and delegate hooks, then share family outer parsing and one-pass accounting. Streaming destinations explicitly require replayable values for right/center alignment.
tradeoffs:
The internal helpers share outer alignment parsing, display-column accounting,
debug defaults and nested formatting. Left-aligned output renders once on any
iterator. Bounded writable pointer buffers also support right/center alignment
in one pass by inserting padding while retaining the exact truncated prefix.
Other iterators require replayable values for right/center alignment; unknown
custom formatters and consuming ranges return `unsupported_type` before invoking
the formatter. These helpers are implementation details, not a public extension
API. Optional formatters should document which input operations are device callable.

title: Adapt standard value wrappers and complex numbers
problem: Format common standard wrappers through existing contained-value formatters.
design: Explicit adapters avoid streams and RTTI; each standard operation must be available on the target.
tradeoffs:
Optional and variant values use debug presentation for contained text; bitsets,
bytes, reference wrappers, atomics, complex numbers, source locations and pointer
views have explicit adapters. `ffmt::ptr` makes a raw/smart pointer printable
without dereferencing it. Atomic formatting loads the current value; a format
call is not an atomic snapshot across multiple arguments. These adapters do not
supply filesystem, streams, RTTI, thread-ID or exception-traversal services.
Standard-library types and their operations must themselves be device callable.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; wrapper/bitset/complex/pointer/rejection tests extracted and grouped. No implementation token change.

title: Format C++23 expected and unexpected values

commands: make test-cxx23 CXX="$CXX" # compiler mode must be C++23; exit 77 is unsupported

problem: Represent expected values and errors when the standard library supports C++23.
design: Separate opt-in header and skip semantics preserve C++20 portability.
tradeoffs:
`std23.hpp` adds `std::expected` and `std::unexpected` adapters when the selected
standard library exposes C++23 expected support. C++20 users can omit the header.
The contained value and error must be formattable. Optional tests report skip
(exit 77) when the standard library lacks the feature; that skip is not evidence
of conformance. Enable the suite with a C++23 compiler mode.

title: Add explicit ANSI color and emphasis wrappers
problem: Request ANSI styling explicitly around an existing formattable value.
design: Typed composition emits deterministic bytes without terminal detection.
tradeoffs:
Styles explicitly emit ANSI escape bytes around the formatted value and reset
when a nonempty style ends. There is no terminal detection; captured output also
contains those bytes. RGB, terminal palette colors and emphasis flags compose
with `operator|`. Incompatible repeated terminal colors report `invalid_format`.
The wrapped formatter still owns ordinary value parsing and width semantics.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout and standalone explicit-style tests/docs. No implementation token change.

title: Add checked typed percent formatting
problem: Support percent formatting without unsafe C varargs or the writing conversion %n.
design: A separate typed grammar shares primitive conversion and bounded sinks, but does not implement %n.
tradeoffs:
The percent parser uses typed arguments rather than C varargs and shares the
bounded output/error contract of brace formatting. It supports positional
arguments, dynamic width/precision, integer length modifiers and narrow/wide
output. Invalid conversions report errors; `%n` is rejected and never writes
through a pointer. Floating arguments follow printf's float-to-double promotion.
This parser is intentionally separate from brace parsing so each grammar can be
reviewed and tested independently.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; all percent-format matrices/arguments/guards retained in named test groups. No implementation token change.

before: Brace formatting does not interpret %#08x; there is no typed percent parser or explicit %n rejection.
